clue.text: Art? I'd concern when it's deviant or sexist?

indicators.note: deviant means straying from the norm, so these letters stray into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A wry question whether an art-world matter turns sexist once it goes off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's deviant' tells you the letters of ART I'D CONCERN are to be rearranged; 'or' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcentric means centred on men, a male-dominated outlook, which is a form of sexism.

clue.text: Fizz put into beer, strangely lactic, getting one enraged

indicators.note: one thing is put into another, so the word for fizz goes inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pop is a fizzy drink

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of lactic come out in an odd, unexpected order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A drinker adds fizz to a beer that tastes oddly of sour milk, and becomes furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' sets the fizzy drink inside the beer, making APOPLE; 'strangely' then shuffles lactic into CTICAL. 'getting one' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplectical is an older form of apoplectic, describing someone so furious they look about to burst.

clue.text: Foreign duck, name applied to foreign goose leaving California

indicators.note: leaving says the abbreviation for California departs from the bird's name

parts.note: the Canada goose takes its name from a foreign country
CA is the US postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A list of exotic waterfowl names, a duck and a goose, with one bird missing from California.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing; Spanish for nothing is NADA. 'leaving' takes California's CA from CANADA, the name given to that goose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nada is the Spanish for nothing, and a duck is a cricket score of zero, so it is a nil in another language.

clue.text: Drummer and old piper played, ready to fall

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for drummer

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of piper are worked over and rearranged like a tune

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A drummer and an old bagpiper perform until they are about to keel over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' signals rearranging the piper's letters into PRIPE; the drummer and old come first as standard abbreviations. Droppripe is a dialect word for ripe fruit about to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Droppripe describes fruit so mature that it is about to drop from the tree of its own accord.

clue.text: Like clean sheets, classically, as penned by artist, English

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, so as goes inside the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An English artist writing about crisp clean bedsheets in a classical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' encloses the little word in the Royal Academician, giving RASA, then E for English. Tabulae rasae are 'clean slates', the Latin plural of tabula rasa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasae is the Latin feminine plural meaning scraped or blank, as in tabulae rasae, unwritten tablets.

clue.text: Fille de joie requiring shelter in bed? The opposite

indicators.note: in places one word within another; read straight it would put the shelter inside the bed
The opposite reverses the order just stated, so the bed goes inside the shelter instead

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for birds or animals, as in dovecote
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A French lady of the night is said to need shelter in bed, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'in' would put the shelter inside the bed; 'The opposite' tells you to swap the roles, so the bed sits inside the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocotte is a French term for a prostitute or kept woman, just as fille de joie is a euphemism for one.

clue.text: Opium component in measure after cocaine's taken in nostril

indicators.note: after says the measure comes later in the answer than the rest
taken in means swallowed up, so the drug abbreviation goes inside the nostril

parts.note: a nare is a nostril (plural nares)
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
an en is a printer's unit of measure

explanation.surface: A drug chemist tracks an opium ingredient measured after cocaine has been snorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts C into the nostril, NARCE, and 'after' places the printer's measure behind it. Nare is an old singular of nares, the nostrils.
explanation.definitionFit: Narceen is an alkaloid found in opium, one of the many chemical constituents of the poppy's latex.

clue.text: Element lacking any surrounding for misanthrope

indicators.note: surrounding says the letters of any removed are those round the outside, the last of them at the far end
lacking says letters of any are missing from the element's name

parts.note: antimony is a chemical element, Sb
the first two letters of any come off the front; its final Y comes off the end

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle about an element with nothing around it, applied to a person who shuns company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking any surrounding' asks for the element whose outer letters spell any; 'lacking' strips the front pair, leaving TIMONY, and 'surrounding' takes the final Y too.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, subject of Shakespeare's play, is the classic hater of humankind.

clue.text: Scots reveal circle between water meadows

indicators.note: between puts the circle in the middle, with one water meadow either side

parts.note: an ing is a meadow by a river, so two of them are ING and ING
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A Scottish revelation about a ring found between riverside meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' sets O between two water meadows. Reveal is the architectural noun: the side of a door or window opening, which in Scots is called an ingoing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, an ingoing is the side of a door or window recess, which architects call the reveal.

clue.text: It has no place in adulthood, changing since one ages

definitions.text: It has no place in adulthood

indicators.note: changing says the letters alter their order, matching the surface theme of growing up

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Something with no place in adult life, which changes as a person grows older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges SINCE ONE AGES. Caenogenesis is the appearance in an embryo or larva of features absent from the adult ancestors.
explanation.definitionFit: Caenogenesis covers developmental features seen only in early stages of life and lost before the organism is mature.

clue.text: Airborne troops about to make earthwork protecting rear

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the troops go round the verb

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
to do something is to make or carry it out

explanation.surface: Paratroopers set about building an earthwork to guard their rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads like 'about to', but here PARAS surround DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A parados is a bank of earth behind a trench, shielding soldiers from fire coming from behind.

clue.text: Healthy hospital opening in Edinburgh

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A healthy new hospital opening in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like a ribbon-cutting; it means the first letter of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sane means sound of mind, and in its older sense sound and healthy in body as well.

clue.text: Island record producers hope to achieve this with backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the phrase for a chart-topper is read in reverse

parts.words: record producers hope to achieve this
parts.note: a No. 1 hit, written A NO I

explanation.surface: Record producers dream of a chart-topper, with a little help from backing singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with backing' sounds like backing vocals, but it means the chart-topper, written A NO. I, is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Goes off the rails, caught with weapon in minor affray once

indicators.note: in places the caught-and-weapon letters inside the rearranged word
off the rails means wildly disordered, so the letters of goes are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone who goes off the rails is caught with a weapon in a small brawl of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the rails' jumbles GOES into SOGE, and 'in' sets caught plus weapon after its S. Scarmoge is a Spenserian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarmoge is an old, Spenserian word for a skirmish, a small-scale fight or scuffle.

clue.text: Fruit dad held in hand

indicators.note: held in says one word is gripped within another

parts.note: paw is an informal word for a hand
pa is another word for dad

explanation.surface: A child holds a piece of fruit given by dad in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' places father inside the informal word for a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaw is a variant spelling of pawpaw, the tropical papaya or the North American custard-apple tree.

clue.text: Biological triplet runs away from police line

indicators.note: something that runs away from a place leaves it, so the letter is removed from the police line

parts.note: a cordon is a line of police holding back a crowd
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Three kids flee from a police cordon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like the verb, but it is R, the cricket abbreviation; 'away from' takes it out of the police line.
explanation.definitionFit: A codon is a sequence of three nucleotides in DNA or RNA that codes for one amino acid.

clue.text: Stallion, as once, learning to take exercise initially

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: first letters of to, take and exercise

explanation.surface: A horse in training learns to take exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives TTE from to, take, exercise. 'Stallion' looks like a horse, but in old slang it meant a courtesan, and a lorette was a Parisian kept woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Stallion is an obsolete word for a courtesan, and a lorette is a fashionable woman of easy virtue.

clue.text: Form of religion: I vote against being introduced to a Chinese one

indicators.note: being introduced to means put inside, so I and the negative vote enter the Chinese people

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
a nay is a vote against
A means one

explanation.surface: A voter rejects one Chinese form of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being introduced to' puts I and the negative vote into the Han people, giving HINAYAN, then A for 'one' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinayana, the 'lesser vehicle', is a name for the conservative schools of Buddhism such as Theravada.

clue.text: Solicitor making millions, gripped by disgust

indicators.note: gripped by says the letter for millions is held inside the word for disgust

parts.note: the pip is a fit of disgust or irritation, as in 'it gives me the pip'

explanation.surface: A lawyer earning millions to general disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripped by' puts M inside the pip. 'Solicitor' looks like a British lawyer, but here it means someone who solicits on behalf of prostitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimp touts for customers for prostitutes, literally soliciting for them in the street.

clue.text: Snub delivered by eastern poem in revolt that's rising (7, two words)

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: a song is a poem or lyric
the people are up when they are in revolt

explanation.surface: A rebuff given by an eastern poem about a rising rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's rising' reads the three pieces upwards in this down answer, giving PUG NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose is short and upturned, the same shape as a pug dog's face.

clue.text: Bread carried on head in travelling baskets

indicators.note: carried on puts the bread on top of the head in this down answer

parts.note: pita is a flat bread
a ras is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: Bread carried on the head in baskets, as street vendors do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried on' means placed above in a down answer. Ras, from Arabic, is a headland, as in many place names; a pitara is a basket used on journeys in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitara is an Indian basket or box used for carrying belongings on a journey.

clue.text: Woggle, might one suppose? It's creating a row

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: a woggle is the ring through which a Scout's neckerchief, a kind of tie, is threaded
second meaning: arranging in tiers, one row above another

explanation.surface: A Scout's neckerchief ring is jokingly analysed while a quarrel brews.
explanation.walkthrough: A woggle is the leather or plastic ring that holds a Scout's neckerchief in place; 'tie ring' describes it fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiering means arranging things in tiers, ranks placed one above another like rows of seats.

clue.text: Climber almost beneath sacred mountain of Aphrodite

indicators.note: beneath puts the climbing plant below the mountain in this down answer

parts.note: Mount Ida, in Crete or near Troy, is sacred in Greek myth

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a liana is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A climber nearly reaches the foot of a holy mountain linked to Aphrodite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts LIANA to LIAN, and 'beneath' sets it under Mount Ida. Idalium in Cyprus was a centre of Aphrodite's worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Idalian relates to Idalium, a Cypriot town where Aphrodite was worshipped, so it describes things belonging to her.

clue.text: Unable to play in key series, i.e. put out breaking record

definitions.text: Unable to play in key series

indicators.note: breaking into a word means splitting it, so the rearranged letters go inside the record

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a record

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A player is out of a key series after breaking a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I.E. PUT into UPTIE, and 'breaking' puts that inside the compact disc. In football a cup-tied player has already played for another club in that cup competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup-tied footballer is barred from a cup competition because they played in it earlier for another club.

clue.text: From e.g. Victori a fool finding himself in Cannongate

indicators.note: finding himself in says the fool is sitting inside the place name

parts.note: the letters n-o-n-g run consecutively through the middle of this place name

explanation.surface: An Australian idiot ends up in Edinburgh's Canongate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding himself in' points to the answer inside canNONGate. 'Victori a' stands for Victoria, the Australian state; nong is Australian slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Nong is Australian slang for an idiot, so it is a dimwit from a place such as Victoria.

clue.text: 'Bright' fool heading intelligence department

indicators.note: heading in a down answer means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
ID is short for intelligence department

explanation.surface: A dim official, ironically called bright, runs the intelligence section.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the fool heads the department while the answer means clever-looking and shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitid is a literary word for shining or glossy, a synonym of bright in its visual sense.

clue.text: A contract

parts.note: this was the month's competition word, so Azed gave only a plain definition of it and no wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: This was the clue-writing competition puzzle: the setter printed only a definition for this entry, and solvers were invited to write their own clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement between parties settling what each gives and receives, which is a contract.

clue.text: Cat, black, on top of tree

indicators.note: on top of in a down answer puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the oak is a tree

explanation.surface: A black cat perched at the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top of' sets B for black above the tree. 'Cat' is not the animal; to cat is to vomit, and boak is the Scots word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Boak is Scots and northern English for retching or vomiting, which is also a slang meaning of cat.

clue.text: Paid pound rent formerly

parts.note: to give money is to pay it, so paid is gave
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone paid a pound for rent in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavel here is not the auctioneer's hammer but an old word for tribute or rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavel is an archaic term for tribute or rent owed to a feudal lord.

clue.text: Crown jewel maybe consistingof less than half a precious stone

parts.note: printed as one word; in means consisting of, as in 'a sum in coins'

parts.words: less than half a precious stone
parts.note: DIA is three of the seven letters of diamond, under half of them

explanation.surface: A crown jewel made of less than half of one precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: India was called 'the jewel in the crown' of the British Empire, hence the 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: India was famously the most prized possession of the British Empire, its jewel in the crown.

clue.text: Money on eBay squandered, perhaps

indicators.note: squandered means scattered wastefully, so the letters of eBay are scattered

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Money frittered away on eBay, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are both adverbs expressing possibility rather than certainty.

clue.text: Club ungraciously accepts such a tip

indicators.note: accepts says the answer is taken in by the words around it

parts.note: the answer spans the end of club and the start of ungraciously

explanation.surface: A club rudely takes a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' shows the answer held within clu-B UNG-raciously; 'such' points back to the ungracious taking. A bung is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is British slang for a bribe or backhander, an illicit tip slipped to someone.

clue.text: Perverse old skill reflected in icon crafted by king

indicators.note: by means next to, so the king follows the rest
in places the reflected skill inside the reworked icon
crafted means worked and shaped, so the letters of icon are reshaped

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the word for skill reads backwards

parts.note: art is skill
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An icon crafted by a king, with skill mirrored in it, turns out to be perverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafted' reorders icon as CONI, 'reflected' reverses the skill to TRA, and 'in' sets it before the I to give CONTRAI; 'by' then adds R for king. Contrair is Scots for contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrair is an archaic or Scots form of contrary, meaning wilfully opposite or obstinate.

clue.text: A ristorante serves this (not rare) bottled

definitions.text: A ristorante serves this (not rare) bottled

indicators.note: serves up suggests the letters are dished out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter
the letters to be removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: An Italian restaurant serves this wine by the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serves' signals the rearrangement: remove the letters of NOT and RARE from A RISTORANTE, leaving A, I, S, T to reorder; the whole clue also describes a bottled Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white wine from Piedmont, which a restaurant would sell by the bottle.

clue.text: Burmese people are born in what may be Indian, backward

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the reversed word
backward says the word for what may be Indian is read in reverse

parts.note: Indian ink is a kind of ink
N is the abbreviation for born (natus)

explanation.surface: Burmese people are born in a place that might be called Indian, backwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns the Indian sort of ink into KNI, and 'in' puts ARE plus N for born inside it after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: The Karenni are an ethnic group of eastern Myanmar, also known as the Red Karen.

clue.text: Juggling trade transactions gladdens, alas, when treated deviously (12, three words)

indicators.note: treated deviously means handled in a twisting way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Juggling trade deals gladdens some and dismays others, when done sneakily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juggling' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the definition; the anagram is signalled by 'when treated deviously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leads and lags are the speeding up or delaying of international payments to profit from expected currency moves.
